what: Cintas rents uniforms and supplies to businesses. It delivers clean uniforms, floor mats, mops and restroom supplies on a weekly route, and sells first aid, safety and fire protection services alongside them.
customers: More than a million businesses of every size in the United States, Canada and Latin America.
money: weekly rental and cleaning of uniforms, mats and towels
restocking first aid cabinets, safety products and training
extinguisher and sprinkler inspection and service
moat: Route density: once a lorry already stops on a street, adding a customer costs almost nothing, which no new entrant can match.
risks: Revenue tracks employment at its customers, since it bills per uniformed worker
Growth is steady but modest in a mature market
The shares trade at a high multiple of earnings
Energy and labour costs affect route profitability
opportunities: Return on invested capital above 25% and consistent price increases make it unusually profitable
Many businesses still handle uniforms in-house, which is the main source of new customers
First aid and fire protection cross-sell into existing routes at higher margins
watch: Organic revenue growth and incremental margin, which show whether route density keeps improving.
